editorial_contributions.text:
The space \(M_n(\mathbb C)\) of complex \(n\times n\) matrices becomes a normed space with the Frobenius norm induced by the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product \(\langle A, B \rangle = \mathrm{tr}(A^*B)\). It is known that the Böttcher-Wenzel inequality \(\| [A,B]\| \le \sqrt{2} \|A\| \|B\|\) is sharp.

The authors study a generalized inner product of the form \(\langle A, B \rangle_\omega = \mathrm{tr}(A^*B\omega)\) which induces a so-called weighted Frobenius norm \(\|A\|_\omega\) where \(\omega\) is a positive definitive matrix. Inequalities of the form \(\| [A,B] \|_{\eta} \le c(\omega) \|A\|_{\eta_A} \|B\|_{\eta_B}\) are studied, where \(\eta, \eta_A, \eta_B\) stands for either \(\omega\) or the identity matrix (there is a total of six such inequalities, one of them being the case with no weight where the sharp bound is known). In two cases the authors show that the bound is sharp. In the three other cases the authors conjecture a sharp bound, prove their conjecture rigorously in the case \(n=2\) and provide numerical simulations for \(n>2\) supporting their conjecture. The given bounds depend only on the largest and the two smallest eigenvalues of \(\omega\).

The results can be applied to quantum mechanics. A state in an \(n\) level quantum system is a positive semidefinite matrix \(\omega\) with unit trace and observables are \(n\times n\) matrix. The variance of an observable \(A\) under the state \(\omega\) is \(V(A)_\omega = \|A - (\mathrm{tr} \omega A) \mathbb I \|_\omega^2\). Therefore, one obtains a new type of uncertainty principle of the form \(V(A)_\omega V(B)_\omega \ge c(\omega) \| [A,B] \|_\omega\). As a second application, the authors show that their bounds lead to constraints on the relaxation rates for quantum Markovian dynamics.

Norms (inequalities, more than one norm, etc.) of linear operators
Selfadjoint operator theory in quantum theory, including spectral analysis
Nonselfadjoint operator theory in quantum theory including creation and destruction operators

title.title: Böttcher-Wenzel inequality for weighted Frobenius norms and its application to quantum physics

editorial_contributions.text:
The Böttcher-Wenzel inequality asserts that \(\|[X,Y]\|^2\le 2\|X\|^2\|Y\|^2\), where \([X, Y] = XY - YX\) denotes the Lie bracket of the \(n\times n\) complex matrices \(X\) and \(Y\). The present paper studies recent conjectures that generalize the Böttcher-Wenzel inequality using the \(\omega\)-weighted Frobenius norm, where \(\omega\) is a positive definite \(n\times n\) matrix with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1 \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n>0\). The \(\omega\)-norm is defined as
\[
\|X\|_\omega = \sqrt{\operatorname{tr}(\omega X^*X)}.
\]
The authors establish several inequalities involving the Lie bracket under various combinations of norms, including:
\begin{align*} 
\|[X, Y]\|_\omega^2 &\le \left( \frac{1}{\lambda_{n-1}} + \frac{1}{\lambda_n} \right) \|X\|_\omega^2 \|Y\|_\omega^2, \tag{1} \\
\|[X, Y]\|_\omega^2 &\le \left( 1 + \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_n} \right) \|X\|_\omega^2 \|Y\|^2 ,\tag{2} \\
\|[X, Y]\|_\omega^2 &\le 2\lambda_1 \|X\|^2 \|Y\|^2, \tag{3} \\
\|[X, Y]\|^2 &\le \frac{1}{\lambda_n} \left( \frac{1}{\lambda_{n-1}} + \frac{1}{\lambda_n} \right) \|X\|_\omega^2 \|Y\|_\omega^2 .\tag{4} 
\end{align*}

The authors prove (1), (2), and (4) for all rank-one matrices \(X\) and \(Y\), and show that the constants in (1) and (2) are optimal. For inequality (3), they determine the \emph{optimal constant} \(C_\omega\) for rank-one matrices, improving upon the known bound. The paper also discusses challenges in determining a sharp constant for (4) and outlines how their approach may contribute to future progress.
